I am 64 years old and I have worked this same 6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and talk with the input dealer, but most of what I know comes from doing the work and watching what happens on my fields and my neighbors' fields.

For the winter wheat, I sow in early October right after the National Day holiday. Last year I switched to an improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang used — he got about 50 jin more per mu than my old seed, and the seed dealer in town also said it does well here. I sow about 45 jin of seed per mu. At sowing time, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kilograms each. The dealer told me that gives 7.5 kilograms of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium per mu. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I topdress with 20 kilograms of urea per mu. At jointing in April, another 15 kilograms of urea per mu. Urea is 46% nitrogen, so the dealer says that is about 16 kilograms of nitrogen from the urea, plus the 7.5 from the compound bag — around 23 or 24 kilograms of nitrogen per mu total. I do not buy separate phosphorus or potassium fertilizer; the compound bag is enough for me. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the autumn is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling in May. The electricity for the well pump costs money, so I do not water more than that. I spray pesticide twice — herbicide right after sowing, and then in spring for aphids and powdery mildew. After the maize comes off, I hire the rotary tiller from the village machine group for 40 yuan per mu to prepare the seedbed.

Summer maize is different — there is no time to waste after wheat harvest in early June. The season is tight, so I direct-seed a hybrid variety with the no-tillage planter, about 3 jin of seed per mu. I learned that if you stop to plow, you might miss the good sowing window and lose yield. At sowing, I put down 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu — again the 15-15-15 type. Then at the big trumpet stage, I side-dress with 25 kilograms of urea per mu. That comes to about 17 or 18 kilograms of nitrogen per mu in total. I irrigate twice — once when the plants are knee-high if it is dry, and once at tasseling. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer and weeds. No tillage for maize — it saves time and saves 40 yuan per mu.

I work this land alone since my wife passed. I am 64 now, so for harvest and peak times I sometimes hire one or two day laborers from the village, maybe 3 or 4 days total per year. Every bag of fertilizer is real cash from my pocket — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now. But I learned long ago that trying to save 50 yuan on fertilizer and then losing 100 jin of grain is stupid math. A bad harvest is a disaster when you are alone; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost you absorb. I would rather put a little too much than too little. I watch what my neighbors do, and if everyone around me is applying roughly this amount, I know I am not far wrong. I expect around 500 kilograms per mu from the wheat if the spring rain is decent, and about 550 kilograms per mu from the maize.
